title: AI and Chat GPT in Language Teaching: Enhancing EFL Classroom Support and Transforming Assessment Techniques
venue: International Journal of Higher Education Pedagogies
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the role of artificial intelligence and Chat GPT in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teaching, focusing on how these tools can support personalized learning, real-time language practice, lesson planning, assessment, and evaluation. Rather than reporting a controlled empirical comparison, it presents a conceptual discussion of how AI can transform language instruction and educational assessment.

The paper argues that AI-powered systems can tailor lessons to learners' needs, provide immediate feedback on grammar, pronunciation, and vocabulary, and help teachers generate lesson plans and learning materials more efficiently. It also describes AI uses in adaptive testing, automated grading, continuous formative assessment, performance analysis, and test security, emphasizing that teachers remain essential for interpretation, judgment, and instructional decision-making.

The context is EFL education, with examples drawn from platforms and tools such as Duolingo, Rosetta Stone, ExamSoft, Grammarly, and university EFL settings. The paper concludes that AI and Chat GPT can enhance language learning and assessment, but their successful use depends on balancing technology with human interaction and addressing ethical issues such as privacy, equity, bias, and access.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative essay/review article rather than an empirical study. It contains no original dataset, comparison design, or statistical analysis of teacher-facing generative AI feedback.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful benefits for EFL teaching, writing support, and grading efficiency, but these are descriptive and not quantified. The practical impact is therefore plausible but unclear from the evidence presented.

interventions.use_case: Chat GPT use in EFL classrooms for real-time language practice, answering student questions, and providing conversational support/feedback to learners and teachers
AI-powered language learning platforms such as Duolingo and Rosetta Stone that adapt lessons and practice to learner performance and pacing
AI-driven automated grading and feedback for written responses, including grammar/spelling correction and coherence suggestions
AI writing assistants and pronunciation/grammar feedback tools for EFL writing and language development
AI-enhanced performance analysis and learning analytics to identify students struggling with topics and guide instructional intervention

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI writing assistants and automated feedback systems improve EFL writing quality by identifying grammar and spelling errors, suggesting revisions, and supporting clearer and more coherent written responses. It cites a case study at New York University reporting substantial improvements in students' written English proficiency, but the article does not report a precise effect size or sample size.
finding.measure: Written English proficiency, grammar/style quality, coherence of student writing

finding.finding_summary: Automated grading and feedback on written assignments are described as helping students learn from mistakes and make necessary improvements. The article presents this as a beneficial application of AI in assessment, but provides no original experimental estimates, effect sizes, or sample information.
finding.measure: Quality of written assignment feedback and revision support

finding.finding_summary: The paper claims that Chat GPT-based chatbots and other AI language tools provide immediate feedback on pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension, improving learners' language proficiency and confidence. These claims are presented through descriptive discussion and cited cases rather than a controlled study, so no effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Pronunciation, grammar usage, vocabulary usage, speaking/conversation practice, language proficiency

finding.finding_summary: AI-powered language learning platforms are described as providing adaptive practice and instant pronunciation feedback that support oral language development. The paper cites Duolingo, Rosetta Stone, and AI-powered apps for young learners as examples, but does not present new comparative data or statistics.
finding.measure: Language proficiency, pronunciation feedback, conversational practice

finding.finding_summary: The paper repeatedly argues that AI-generated lesson plans, automated grading, and chatbot support reduce teacher workload and save time in planning and assessment. This is a descriptive claim supported by examples such as Chat GPT assisting teachers and ExamSoft streamlining grading, but no empirical effect size is provided.
finding.measure: Teacher workload, planning time, grading efficiency

finding.finding_summary: AI-enhanced examination software is described as improving grading consistency, speeding up assessment, and increasing test security through automated proctoring. The paper treats these as practical efficiency gains, but offers no quantitative evaluation of time saved or error reduction.
finding.measure: Grading speed, assessment efficiency, test security processes

finding.finding_summary: The article emphasizes ethical concerns including privacy, equity, access, and bias as central consequences of AI adoption in education. It does not test institutional outcomes experimentally, but argues that AI can widen or narrow access depending on implementation and governance.
finding.measure: Privacy, equity/access, algorithmic bias, responsible AI governance
